Like Jess McClain, I Took Time Off From Running—and Came Back Stronger. These Signs Mean It’s Time to Step Away.

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1687 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Runnersworld

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • They say distance makes the heart grow fonder, and that’s true for me with running.
  • Recent findings suggest that around this time last year, I went from lifting two to three days a week while training for my first marathon to stopping workouts completely and struggling to get off my couch.
  • Professional distance runner and Upcoming York City Marathon runner-up Jess McClain previously told Runner’s World she felt similarly about six years ago.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

They say distance makes the heart grow fonder, and that’s true for me with running. But by “distance,” I don’t mean bumping up my mileage or running farther. I mean taking time and space away from my sport during seasons when I feel burned out, lost, or simply exhausted.

Recent findings suggest that around this time last year, I went from lifting two to three days a week while training for my first marathon to stopping workouts completely and struggling to get off my couch. The second I crossed the finish line, all I wanted to do was let my running shoes collect dust, avoid my local trail, and avoid stepping foot in the gym for a while.

Professional distance runner and Upcoming York City Marathon runner-up Jess McClain previously told Runner’s World she felt similarly about six years ago. At that time, she consistently stopped hitting her paces in her workouts and decided to step back from running—a break that lasted about two years.

It has been revealed that in my case, I wasn’t as decisive. For months, I resisted the idea that I needed to take a break.

It has been revealed that I’d heard that a month is generally how long you need to recover from a marathon, so I told myself that’s when I would jump into winter base training. But every time I tried to get back out there, I got bored and I struggled to recover from my runs. I waited until summer for the urge to work out again, but it never really came back.

Industry observers note that for a while, I felt like getting burned out was my fault, that I must have pushed too hard in training. Looking back now—and with help from an expert—I understand that my break was exactly what I needed to get back to my sport in a sustainable way.

According to recent reports, my break from running lasted about nine months, and I came back feeling like the runner I had always been before. Plus, I raced one of my fastest half marathons as my comeback.

Below I offer the telltale signs it’s time for a break from running, what a “break” really means, and the benefits you can gain from stepping away from the sport for a while—even if it seems impossible to do so at first.

The farther away I got from my training cycle, the more I realized how much I overtrained. I’d been strength training for 90 minutes three times a week with heavy weights while balancing 30-plus-mile weeks and 20-mile long runs. As I gained more perspective after my race ended, I noticed signs that I was in desperate need of a break.

Industry observers note that “Pay attention to trends and patterns [throughout your training],” Erin Ayala, PhD, a sports psychologist, certified mental performance consultant, and founder of Skadi Sport Psychology, tells Runner’s World. “We all have bad days where the numbers aren’t coming together or a run feels harder than it normally does at a given pace. But if it continues to occur, then it can definitely be a sign to take a break,” she says.

Ayala says there are three main factors that often lead to athletic burnout. Here’s what each can look like, and how I experienced them.

You might need to take a step back if you find yourself hitting training plateaus despite putting in your best efforts.

I picked a training blueprint that included paces far too fast for my fitness level at the time, so every interval workout I did felt difficult, and my paces never really improved. The longer the intervals got, the farther I was from my desired split. But I kept checking off the weekly workouts anyway.

According to recent reports, this lack of personal achievement and growth can halt your motivation levels. “When you’re not able to progress and you lose sight of [personal achievements] you’re just going through the motions, that’s a really massive red flag,” Ayala notes.

Recent findings suggest that after the first month or so, marathon training started to feel more like a chore and I felt really tired and disconnected during my workouts. I figured it was probably normal because I had never run a marathon before, but it turns out that’s not how you should expect to feel daily in your training. “If the workouts are just a grind and you’re having to peel yourself off of the couch in order to get them in, and that’s a sustained pattern, then that’s another big red flag,” Ayala notes.

In a recent development, A change in my relationship with running and my “why” meant grappling with my identity as a runner, which Ayala says is the third factor that can contribute to athletic burnout. You might ask yourself questions like, “Why do I even do this anymore?” and “What’s the point?” She says that if those questions linger for more than a week or so, then that’s a sign you might need a break.

By the time I got to the start line, I questioned why I was even there, and all I could do was get through it. “There’s a very real sense of grief and loss, and that’s really scary,” when taking a step back from running, Ayala explains. “Often we hang on quite desperately to our athletic identity when it’s also okay to move on and to do something different.”.

Once I knew I needed a break from running, I didn’t quite know how to hit pause.

According to recent reports, then Ayala pointed out that perfectionism can affect your relationship with your sport. And simply hearing that helped me realize why I needed to step away.

There are two types of perfectionists, Ayala explains. The first type is the high achiever, who wants to be the best and perform at the top as much as possible. The second type of perfectionist takes a more “maladaptive form.” These individuals are highly motivated by others’ perceptions and expectations, she notes. They might fear failure and generally don’t want to disappoint people.

Industry observers note that that second type of perfectionism resonated with me because I realized I was listening to a nagging voice in my head that expected me to give absolutely everything I had to my training. And if I didn’t, I would face that critical voice’s judgment and let it fill me with disappointment and shame.

“Breaks can be helpful because they essentially force you to turn that perfectionistic tendency off. They’re a good way to keep yourself balanced,” Ayala adds.

Once I knew this and decided to take a break, I figured out how to fill my time.

Those first few months after marathon training, I was so excited to not think about running at all. Instead, I looked forward to filling my free time by rebooting my old Webkinz account (an online virtual-pet game popular in the mid-2000s), decorating my new apartment, and watching a lot of TV.

“First, just give yourself time. Then, you can create other bite-sized goals like daily movement, getting outside, spending time with friends, or exploring different hobbies,” Ayala suggests.

When I passed the two-month mark of my break, I took up pottery classes. While that hobby didn’t last, it gave me the space I needed from running.

I knew, deep down, that rest was probably what I needed. But when I took time off, I felt too anxious and ashamed to even enjoy it: I kept thinking about how much time I was wasting and how out-of-shape I felt. “The problem [with athletic burnout] isn’t that you just need to motivate yourself harder. You need to rest in order to get that intrinsic motivation back,” Ayala states.

Ayala explains that if we lose our intrinsic motivation, we often rely on feelings of shame and discipline to keep up with our routine, which ultimately isn’t sustainable.

When I was honest with myself, I found my fresh “why” for running—my intrinsic motivator—and that was because of how strong, creative, and capable it makes me feel.

In a recent development, one piece of advice from Ayala especially resonates with me: Accept where you’re at and normalize taking a break. “I would argue that getting burned out is a very normal and expected part of being an athlete,” she says. “If you are an athlete long enough, you are going to get burned out at some point and that’s okay. It doesn’t mean that you’re doing something wrong.”.

Industry observers note that once I accepted that I was dealing with a longer-term case of burnout and some depression, I began to see light at the end of the tunnel. I set bite-sized goals, per Ayala’s suggestion, and began by committing to running just five minutes a day for a month. With that, running clicked for me again.

Recent findings suggest that looking back on my time away from running, I don’t view it with shame or anxiety anymore. I see it as both a period of my life when I learned about myself as an athlete and about how my brain works. It was also a time of physiological and mental recovery from so much training stress.

Recent findings suggest that by stepping away, I unlocked a upcoming life experience that can help inform me if—and probably when—I experience burnout again. That perspective shift alone lifts so much weight off my shoulders.

Plus, I’ve come back to the sport now feeling refreshed. I ran one of my fastest half marathons and feel ready to tackle another training strategy. I have the drive to set and achieve goals again. And that’s an irreplaceable benefit to taking some time away.

You can find her wearing purple, baking cupcakes, and visiting her local farmers market.

Industry observers note that even though I finally embraced wearing leggings last year, I still hesitate when it comes to winterizing my running gear—even when the “feels like” temp is 28 degrees Fahrenheit on a 34-degree day. The simplest gear that transforms my getup, doesn’t make me regret overdressing, and helps me stay warm when the weather begins taking its nippy turn? Gloves. My pair of choice is the Smartwool Active Fleece Insulated.

It has been revealed that of all the runs and races I’ve underdressed for, the one accessory I always regret not putting on is a pair of gloves. I’m the kind of person whose hands are constantly cold. (Healthcare friends, I’m sorry for having fingers that refuse to get a quick oxygen read.).

In a recent development, I could go the mitts route, and I do when I need an extra layer over my gloved fingers (yes, I double up). But the thing about running, especially when you’re training for Boston in the spring, is that you need to be able to spread your 10 digits and use them to retrieve fuel—or lip balm or a Kleenex—from the depths of your pockets, which requires more dexterity than mittens allow.

I like Smartwool’s gloves because of their range of sizes, though I will admit the extra small is still slightly long in the tips due to their unisex sizing. The gloves are double-layer knit and have a blend of merino wool and polyester to thermoregulate your hands and wick away sweat. The overlay panels serve as windproof protection.

Recent findings suggest that besides warmth and the usage of my fingers, the Active Fleece also provides visibility, thanks to a reflective logo and piping on the back of the hand. Being seen is key when daylight hours are shorter and I need to log that run before dawn or can only fit in a workout at dusk.

The index and thumb have touchscreen-compatible pads. I wouldn’t recommend them for long-winded texts since, through my own experience, messages aren’t always accurate. But it’s nice that I can type into Google Maps or use dictation and send, “PICK ME UP—I MADE A HORRIBLE MISTAKE” with a location pin.

Sometimes the best test is when you’re not running. On our first chilly morning this fall, I got up early on a Sunday and waited to cheer at mile 10 of a half marathon. The precursor to the waiting was pacing every block in a half-mile radius, trying to figure out if I was actually on the race course.

When the runners came in and I finally found the right sidewalk corner, the stutter in my voice told me I should have worn two extra layers. Despite my frozen core, I was surprised I still had the feeling in my Smartwool gloved hands.

In a recent development, the best part of that morning besides being able to type out post-cheer coffee shop directions? Sticking it out so I could encourage runners with more cowbell.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that whether you’re starting your fitness journey or you’re a weightlifting junkie, there are several supplements that should be staples in your stack. As a certified personal trainer and nutrition coach, I’d put a high-quality whey protein powder and one of the best creatines at the top.

Not far behind would be another supplement that can help you achieve your muscle-building and weight-loss goals: pre-workout.

However, just like not all barbells are created equal, neither are supps. The strongest pre-workouts stand out from the pack because they are formulated with research-backed doses of four key ingredients — caffeine (at least 200 milligrams), L-citrulline (at least 4,000 milligrams), beta-alanine (at least 3,200 milligrams), and betaine (at least 2,500 milligrams) — for physical and mental performance enhancement.

Recent findings suggest that to save you the trouble of sipping on something that won’t give you an effective muscle pump, our team of expert product testers tried more than 80 pre-workouts and reported which supplements delivered the most focus, power, and tingles. Then, with some guidance from a few other experts, our squad of CPTs, CNCs, CrossFit enthusiasts, and dedicated weightlifters narrowed down the list to the eight strongest pre-workouts so you can select the perfect match for your goals and preferences.

Medical disclaimer: This content is meant to be informative, but should not be taken as medical advice. It is not intended for use as diagnosis, prevention, or treatment of health problems. Always speak with your doctor before starting any newly introduced supplement or exercise regimen.

If your goal is to improve your athletic performance and power output in the gym, then we recommend Transparent Labs BULK BLACK. This supplement contains a potent combination of 4,000 milligrams of beta-alanine, 2,500 milligrams of betaine anhydrous, and 10 other active ingredients. Beta-alanine, a nonessential amino acid, may improve potential power output by reducing muscle fatigue, allowing you to push out a few more reps while you exercise. And studies show betaine anhydrous may improve muscular endurance. These ingredients work together to enhance your training, paving the way for strength gains over time.

Industry observers note that each serving of BULK BLACK also contains 350 milligrams of caffeine, which is close to the recommended daily limit of 400 milligrams. Overall, the impressive formulation earns 4 out of 5 stars from our team, as we docked a point for the high caffeine content since it may be too intense for some people.

However, this high-stim pre-workout is certainly effective.

Cory Kessler, C.P.T., C.F.N.C., has tried more than 25 pre-workouts. He tested the Blue Raspberry flavor of BULK BLACK before a cardio workout, noting that he felt more energized and focused throughout his workout. “I started sweating almost immediately, and within five to 10 minutes, I had a boost of energy, a massive pump, and felt like I could lift harder and stronger,” he says. Cory also experienced the tingling sensation common with high doses of beta-alanine.

Cory also enjoys using BULK BLACK before bodybuilding workouts since it contains 8,000 milligrams of citrulline malate. While more research is needed, some studies suggest citrulline malate may boost exercise and muscular performance.

In a recent development, two other areas where BULK BLACK stands out: solubility and taste. Our team gave Transparent Labs perfect scores in both categories.

“BULK BLACK completely dissolved in my shaker bottle in only a few seconds with no clumps, grittiness, or residue,” Cory states.

Available in eight flavors ranging from Black Cherry to Watermelon Peach to Strawberry Mango, one of our other product testers chose the Blue Raspberry option, giving it 5 out of 5 stars for taste. However, there are some mixed reviews on Amazon about the taste, depending on which flavor you choose.

Recent findings suggest that “It’s hard to describe the taste of Blue Raspberry, but that’s exactly what it tastes like. Not too sweet, which is a good thing,” he claims.

Related: Transparent Labs BCAA Glutamine Review.

Legion Pulse is our pick for the strongest natural pre-workout because it’s free from artificial sweeteners, flavors, and colors and contains six active ingredients that support enhanced energy.

It has been revealed that as a CPT and CNC, I look for four main ingredients in a high-quality pre-workout supplement: caffeine, beta-alanine, betaine anhydrous, and L-citrulline. Each plays a key role in enhancing athletic performance. Research reveals:.

Legion Pulse contains all four, including 350 milligrams of caffeine per serving, which is very close to the recommended daily limit of 400 milligrams. Keep in mind that if you decide to try Pulse, it’s a good idea to monitor your caffeine intake from other sources like coffee or tea.

It has been revealed that “To get the most out of pre-workout supplements without stomach complications, start with a lower dose to see how your body reacts,” notes Dr. Christopher Mohr, Ph.D., RD. “Choose supplements with fewer stimulants if caffeine bothers you, or go for stimulant-free options.”.

Luckily, if you’re latest to pre-workout or are caffeine-sensitive, you can also choose the non-stim version of Pulse. So, even though we’d like to see creatine in the formulation, we still give this a strong score of 4 out of 5 stars, especially since there’s a caffeine-free version.

One of our product testers has tried five different brands of pre-workout and puts Pulse atop her list because of its effectiveness.

Recent findings suggest that “I’ve been using Pulse three times a week for six months, and it always makes me feel energized and focused,” our tester indicates. “My goal is to improve my personal records and lift harder, so Pulse is my go-to when I train.”.

According to recent reports, she reports that it typically takes 15 minutes for this high-stim pre-workout to kick in, and while it does give her tingles, it’s not overwhelming. “I never feel a drop-off, but rather a slow energy release,” she claims.

It has been revealed that pulse comes in 22 flavors, including Pink Lemonade, Cherry Limeade, and Strawberry Kiwi, so there’s something to satisfy everyone’s taste buds. That said, one of our testers gave Pulse 4 out of 5 stars for taste, noting that while it tastes sweet, there’s a “weird aftertaste.”.

Sources indicate that while the formulation and flavor options make this a top-rated pre-workout, Pulse is by no means a budget-friendly option. At around $45 for a 20-serving tub, it earns the lowest score of 1 out of 5 stars for price per serving.

While many strong pre-workouts cost around $2 per serving, Nutricost Pre-X is our pick for the strongest budget pre-workout because it costs less than half of that. At about $0.93 per serving, one tester called it “the best value on the market,” and I agree, giving this a perfect score of 5 out of 5 for price per serving.

It has been revealed that although some budget pre-workouts lack key ingredients, Pre-X contains the four main ones we like to see in a pre-workout: caffeine, beta-alanine, betaine anhydrous, and L-citrulline. “The price is better than most other pre-workouts I’ve tried, especially for a supplement this good,” says one tester.

Each serving of Pre-X has 300 milligrams of caffeine and 4,000 milligrams of L-citrulline, so you should feel energized and get a good pump with this pre-workout. “I got a decent pump and had a calm focus without feeling overstimulated,” one tester says.

Some testers say Pre-X has a slightly lower dosage of beta-alanine than some other pre-workouts on our list, but others say they experienced noticeable tingles during their workout.

Industry observers note that while testers did not experience any negative side effects when trying Pre-X, this pre-workout is made with the artificial sweetener sucralose. Some health experts have raised concerns about taking sucralose in high doses. As a CPT and someone who pays close attention to everything I put in my body, I tend to steer clear of artificial sweeteners. Because of this, we docked a point off the formulation score, giving Pre-X 4 out of 5 stars.

Nutricost Pre-X comes in five flavors, including Blue Raspberry, Peach Mango, and Watermelon. Collectively, our team gave this strong pre-workout 4.5 out of 5 stars for taste.

Recent findings suggest that “This tastes great ice cold or at room temperature. I look forward to drinking it before my workouts,” says one tester who tried Blue Raspberry.

Another tester who tried Peach Mango also gave Pre-X his stamp of approval.

According to recent reports, “No artificial sweetener taste at all. It has a nice flavor that’s not overly sweet.”.

Whether you like a strong pre-workout that’s sweet, sour, fruity, or tart, Jacked Factory NitroSurge has a fit for you. With 11 options, you can stick to your favorite or keep a few flavors in rotation to keep your taste buds on their proverbial toes. Between the deep lineup and satisfying flavors, NitroSurge earned a perfect score for taste.

One of our testers tried Strawberry Margarita, and let’s just say she was more than satisfied with her sipping experience.

“It’s wildly delicious. I’d drink this by the side of the pool over ice all day.”.

According to recent reports, another tester prefers Jacked Factory NitroSurge to some other strong pre-workouts he’s tried. “I did not like the Pink Lemonade flavor of Legion Pulse, but I would definitely use the Grape NitroSurge again,” he indicates.

As for its effectiveness? For one of our product testers, it took about 20 minutes to feel NitroSurge kick in. At that point, he felt like he could lift harder.

“I usually work out in the morning because I feel most rested then, but even after taking this in the afternoon, I felt ‘jacked up’ and ready to go,” he says, adding that he experienced tingles and a slight drop off, but neither was overwhelming.

Industry observers note that another tester who regularly takes strong pre-workouts doubled the dosage. He stated he got “a bit of a boost from it” but nothing like what you’ll get from other strong pre-workouts. Ultimately, this makes NitroSurge a solid choice for beginners, as you can see how you respond to a single serving before upping it to two scoops.

Besides the taste, I like that it’s budget-friendly while still including evidence-backed ingredients, like L-citrulline, beta-alanine, betaine anhydrous, caffeine anhydrous, L-theanine, theobromine, and AstraGin. AstraGin, also found in Transparent Labs BULK BLACK, is a plant-based compound formulated to enhance nutrient absorption. While AstraGin is safe at 0.5 milligrams per kilogram of body weight per day, more research is needed on the potential performance-enhancing benefits.

In a recent development, like some of the other pre-workouts on our list, NitroSurge is made with the artificial sweetener sucralose, which some health experts have raised concerns about taking in high doses. Also, Jacked Factory supplements do not undergo third-party testing, which ensures products include the ingredients listed on the label and nothing else. This is especially key for athletes who undergo drug testing for banned substances. We only gave Nitrosurge 3 out of 5 stars in this category since it is made in a Current Good Manufacturing Practice (cGMP)-certified and FDA-registered facility.

According to recent reports, for bodybuilders, a “pump” is a sign of a successful training session. Increased blood flow to the muscles makes them feel fuller and appear larger and more vascular during and after a workout. A pump also promotes muscle growth by delivering essential nutrients and oxygen to the muscles as blood flow increases. While you can achieve a pump through high-rep sets, drop sets, and supersets, high-stim pre-workouts like Gorilla Mode are specially designed to improve your pump.

In a recent development, gorilla Mode contains several pump-enhancing ingredients in each scoop, including 5,000 milligrams of pure L-citrulline (more per scoop than any other pre-workout on our list) and 2,000 milligrams of Hydro Prime glycerol powder. L-citrulline works to widen blood vessels, increasing blood flow to the muscles. Glycerol powder is rapidly absorbed by the muscles and draws in water, which can cause muscle cell swelling.

In a recent development, if you’re caffeine-sensitive or budget-conscious, this intense pre-workout may not be the best for you. Although one serving only contains 200 milligrams of caffeine, you will need to take two servings to get research-backed doses of some key ingredients, including creatine monohydrate (only 2.5 gram per serving). At that point, you’d be at 400 milligrams of caffeine, which is the total amount the FDA indicates is safe for adults to consume per day. For this reason, we docked a point off the formulation, giving Gorilla Mode 4 out of 5 stars in this category.

According to recent reports, don’t forget that this also impacts how much bang you get for your buck. A 40-serving tub costs $60, and you’ll end up going through it that much quicker if you take two scoops before your training sessions. That would bring the cost to $3 per serving. So, from a value standpoint, we can only give Gorilla Mode 2.5 out of 5 stars.

On the other hand, this pricey supplement earned a strong score of 4.5 out of 5 stars for its effectiveness. One of our testers uses strong pre-workouts several times a week and tried Gorilla Mode before an upper-body workout. “Not only did I have a good pump, I also felt more focused. I knocked out a few more reps than usual during my workout,” he says. “I like the Fruit Punch flavor, although it was sweeter than I thought it would be.”.

While our tester enjoyed Gorilla Mode’s taste, he says the powder was gritty and difficult to mix properly. This is likely due to the glycerol powder, which absorbs moisture, leading to clumping.

If you like feeling skin tingles after taking your pre-workout, check out Crazy Nutrition Intensive Pre-Train. I love the prickly skin sensation because it lets me know my pre-workout is kicking in and it’s time to train. This temporary side effect, called paresthesia, is caused by beta-alanine, which works to increase muscular endurance.

It has been revealed that intensive Pre-Train has 3,500 milligrams of beta-alanine per serving, which is more per serving than almost all of the other pre-workouts on our list. “Beta-alanine is found in most pre-workout supplements, likely because it helps reduce fatigue and improve endurance in the short term,” says registered dietitian Alex Oskian. “This is because it reduces acidity in the body, which comes from lactic acid build-up.”.

It has been revealed that our product tester used Crazy Nutrition Intensive Pre-Train before a high-intensity interval training (HIIT) workout and felt the tingles within 15 minutes. “These were strong compared to some other pre-workouts I’ve tried,” he states. “I felt good tingles in my hands and face, which lasted for about an hour.”.

In a recent development, earning a 5 out of 5 for effectiveness, Intense Pre-Train is also available in a caffeine-free version for those who don’t want stimulants in their pre-workout. The non-stim version comes in Green Apple, which our tester says tasted more like a greens powder than a sour apple.

“I’m rather caffeine-dependent, so I didn’t feel a burst of energy. I prefer caffeinated pre-workouts, but this is a great option for a late-night lifting session,” she claims. Other testers who tried the Fruit Punch flavor say they enjoyed the tangy taste. To enhance the flavor, Crazy Nutrition is sweetened with the artificial sweetener sucralose. With some mixed reviews on the different flavors, we give this pre-workout a 3.5 out of 5 for taste.

It has been revealed that onnit Alpha Brain is designed to increase mental acuity and focus. Testers say that’s exactly how they felt after trying Onnit Alpha Brain, which is why it’s our pick for the strongest pre-workout for focus.“What makes this pre-workout stand out is the cognitive effects. I felt significantly more focused after taking Alpha Brain than any other pre-workout I’ve tried,” says one of our testers.

Other testers agreed, saying Alpha Brain helped them feel present and ready to work out without being overstimulated, leading to an effectiveness score of 4 out of 5 stars.

Onnit Alpha Brain’s formula differs from most other strong pre-workout supplements on our list — it contains nootropics, substances that enhance learning and memory. One of the key ingredients, NooGandha, is an ashwagandha extract that can reduce stress and enhance well-being by reducing cortisol levels in the body.

In a recent development, another key ingredient, AlphaSize, may promote the production of acetylcholine, a powerful neurotransmitter that enhances cognitive function. However, studies demonstrating the effect of alpha-GPC on cognitive performance used 200 to 400 milligram doses per day, and a serving of Onnit Alpha brain has 125 milligrams.

In a recent development, the other unique ingredient in Onnit Alpha Brain is Dynamine. It works similarly to caffeine, by blocking the body’s adenosine receptors that cause you to feel tired. However, this ingredient is banned in all sports supplements in Australia. While Dynamine is still allowed for sports competitions in the U.S., it is possible it will be banned in the future. Competitive athletes may want to steer clear of this product.

Sources indicate that one of our testers says Alpha Brain is only middle-of-the-road compared to other strong pre-workouts when it comes to physical energy. “After taking other strong pre-workouts, I usually experience a boost in energy. After taking this pre-workout, the mental effects were much more noticeable than the physical ones,” she says. That may be in part because Alpha Brain lacks ingredients like betaine anhydrous, taurine, and creatine, which can support muscle growth and recovery.

According to recent reports, we give the formulation 4 out of 5 stars thanks to the inclusion of nootropics, which are swiftly becoming more prevalent in the supplement market. But be aware that this probably isn’t your best bet for boosting your physical energy levels.

Long before the days of gummy and ready-to-drink (RTD) pre-workout options, the most popular choice was the original C4. The latest version, C4 Ultimate, is more concentrated than the classic formula, combining both exercise performance and cognitive-enhancing ingredients.

One of our testers tried C4 Ultimate before a 30-minute HIIT workout, reporting that the caffeine blend got her zoned in before her training.

“I felt great throughout the entire workout,” she reported, giving C4 Ultimate a perfect score for effectiveness.

According to recent reports, this high-stim pre-workout is sweetened with sucralose, which some health experts have raised concerns about. While our tester doesn’t mind a very sweet pre-workout, the Icy Blue Razz flavor was a little too sugary for her liking. Mixing it in more water than recommended balances out the sweetness.

However, another tester was blown away by the Sour Batch Bros flavor, saying it tasted “just like Sour Patch Kids.” Taking both of their experiences into consideration, we’ll meet in the middle and give C4 Ultimate a 4 out of 5 for taste, especially since it comes in multiple flavors.

In a recent development, another plus for this product: It contains creatine — a popular supplement among athletes and bodybuilders for its ability to boost strength, enhance recovery, and prevent injury. Because of its performance-enhancing capabilities, some people like to take creatine in addition to their pre-workout. If you want the best of both worlds, we recommend C4 Ultimate.

It has been revealed that keep in mind that one serving contains 1.5 grams of creatine per serving, which is less than the recommended value of 3 to 5 grams daily. If you want to get the most performance-enhancing benefits from creatine, you should invest in a standalone supplement to help support your fitness goals.One final note: If you compete in a sport that requires drug testing, C4 Ultimate may not be the best strong pre-workout for you because it’s made with Dynamine, which is at the moment banned for use in Australia.

Our team of expert testers includes certified personal trainers, nutrition coaches, and CrossFit enthusiasts. As dedicated lifters and lovers of all things health and fitness, we’ve collectively tried more than 80 pre-workouts, giving us a broad perspective of what’s available on the market.

We tested each supplement before a workout, and in some cases, for several weeks or months, to evaluate its performance-enhancing benefits, taste, and whether the supplement had any negative side effects.

Using a 1-5 scoring system, we rated each pre-workout on a variety of factors, including:.

Recent findings suggest that at the end of the testing period, we compared feedback to whittle our list down to only the best of the best. We also received valuable input from nutrition experts on what makes a strong pre-workout.

A strong pre-workout contains a combination of performance-enhancing ingredients in research-backed dosages. “Usually, the strength of a pre-workout is based upon the amount of stimulants it contains. High doses of caffeine (300+ milligrams) are usually a quick identifier of the pre-workout’s strength,” registered dietitian Alex Oskian says.

However, the potency of a pre-workout goes beyond the caffeine content. Other active ingredients like L-citrulline, beta-alanine, and betaine anhydrous can impact energy, focus muscular endurance, and power output.

“Stronger via the amount of caffeine isn’t always better. If the goal is a bigger pump in the gym, other ingredients like L-citrulline may be better,” notes Alex. “Another common ingredient that can help a pre-workout feel stronger is beta-alanine, which may cause a tingling or ‘pins and needles’ sensation on the skin.”.

Recent findings suggest that it’s also vital to remember that “strong” is a subjective term. For example, I can handle a full scoop of RedCon1 Total War without a problem, but I have friends who get too many tingles from a single serving.

According to recent reports, “Everyone’s body reacts differently to various compounds, so what works for one person might not be best for another,” claims Dr. Christopher Mohr, Ph.D., RD.

A strong, well-dosed pre-workout supplement may help you train harder by boosting your energy, focus, and endurance during intense workouts.

“There are a few things that are really helpful when you are looking for a great gym session: energy to do the work, mental clarity to help focus on what you are doing (not just to work the muscle, but to prevent injury), and a great workout,” registered dietitian Alex Oskian says. “Using a pre-workout may just help you achieve all of these.”.

Let’s explore the potential benefits of taking a strong pre-workout before you start your training session.

In a recent development, caffeine is one of the most popular stimulants used in pre-workout supplements to enhance energy levels and improve focus. Almost all of the pre-workouts on our list use caffeine and L-theanine. Studies have shown when paired with caffeine, L-theanine may improve cognitive performance.

“Most pre-workouts contain the stimulant caffeine in higher dosages. L-theanine helps counteract the unwanted effects of caffeine supplementation: jittery feelings and a post-caffeine crash,” Alex notes. “You might see less mental fatigue, improved reaction time, and fewer headaches while regularly supplementing with L-theanine.”.

Recent findings suggest that I like taking a pre-workout to improve my focus because it helps intensify my workout and keep me #lockedin. Several pre-workouts on our list contain Alpha-GPC and tyrosine to give you that zoned-in feeling. Research suggests Alpha-GPC may improve cognitive function, and tyrosine may increase dopamine levels and cognition. One study found L-tyrosine helped improve people’s memory while they worked on a demanding task.

Recent findings suggest that A pre-workout may help you squeeze out a few more reps as you work to build strength and muscle. Two ingredients commonly used in pre-workout, beta-alanine and betaine anhydrous, may help reduce fatigue and support muscular endurance.

According to recent reports, “Research suggests betaine anhydrous can improve muscle strength and power via increased total work capacity and improved protein synthesis within the body. Simply put, you can do more work, which leads to increased strength and muscle growth,” claims Alex.

Another common ingredient, taurine, may improve your performance and power.

Registered dietitian Alex Oskian notes not every pre-workout is created equal, so it’s vital to pay attention to what’s on the label. “Supplements are not regulated by the Food and Drug Administration (FDA). This means the supplement might not contain all the ingredients you’re looking for and may even contain unwanted ingredients,” she says. Alex recommends looking for supplements that undergo third-party testing.

In a recent development, if you choose a high-stim pre-workout, be mindful of your caffeine intake from other sources like coffee, tea, or soda so that you don’t go over the daily recommended value of 400 milligrams. This will help prevent potential negative side effects like jitters, anxiety, or trouble falling asleep.

“Consuming caffeine at the end of your day may cause sleep disturbances, which only hurts performance in the long run,” claims Oskian.

No matter which pre-workout you choose, it’s key to follow the recommended intake guidelines. Remember, pre-workouts should not be taken more than once per day.

In a recent development, “Pre-workout supplements are generally safe for healthy adults, but they can have some potential side effects,” says Dr. Raj Dasgupta, MD, FACP, FCCP, FAASM. “It is key to start with a low dose and talk to your doctor before taking them, especially if you have any underlying health conditions.”.

There are a number of important factors to consider when deciding which strong pre-workout is right for you, including:.

According to recent reports, many strong pre-workouts incorporate a variety of active ingredients. When choosing a pre-workout supplement, consider your goals. For example, a bodybuilder may prefer a pre-workout powder that’s highly caffeinated and contains ingredients such as L-citrulline, betaine anhydrous, and creatine to help improve performance. On the other hand, an endurance athlete may want a pre-workout that has less caffeine but includes beta-alanine, BCAAs, and mineral electrolytes.

In a recent development, whenever possible, I choose supplements that are tested by a third party for purity and have transparent labeling. Athletes who undergo drug testing should look for certifications from Informed Choice and NSF, which ensure the product does not include any banned substances.

Sources indicate that although we test all of the products we recommend, it’s notable to check out customer reviews, especially from people with similar fitness goals and preferences. They can provide valuable insights into the product’s overall effectiveness, potential side effects, and the most popular flavors.

In a recent development, “Recommended brands and products are ones that are highly rated by users and contain ingredients that have been backed by scientific research,” claims Dr. Raj Dasgupta.

In a recent development, “Taste plays a significant role in pre-workout selection. If you don’t like a particular flavor, then you likely won’t drink the pre-workout no matter its benefits,” Oskian says. It’s also crucial to consider the use of artificial flavors, colors, and sweeteners.

The price of a pre-workout doesn’t necessarily reflect its effectiveness. Understanding the ingredients list and dosage levels is important to ensure you’re paying for a high-quality supplement and not just expensive marketing.

There are a few potential red flags you want to avoid when picking out a pre-workout.

In a recent development, I like to avoid supplements made using proprietary blends. These blends are combinations of ingredients, but the individual doses are not fully disclosed. This lack of transparency makes it impossible to assess the effectiveness and safety of the supplement.

It has been revealed that many fitness enthusiasts and athletes prefer all-natural ingredients and products free from unnecessary fillers or additives. “If sugar alcohols and artificial sweeteners wreak havoc on your stomach, make sure those aren’t on the ingredient list,” registered dietitian Alex Oskian claims.

Athletes who compete in sanctioned organizations should make sure the supplements they use are third-party tested and certified banned substance-free.

Industry observers note that if you have massive fitness goals, choosing a strong pre-workout formulated with safe and effective doses of science-backed ingredients is worth it to deliver performance-enhancing effects. Keep in mind that even the strongest pre-workouts on the market won’t make you run faster, lift heavier, or exercise longer on their own. These supplements are designed to help you put in the work at the gym to make gains and enhance your performance over time.

Ultimately, though, a strong pre-workout is only part of the equation to becoming the strongest version of yourself. At the end of the day, you have to put in the work, follow a sound nutrition proposal, and prioritize rest and recovery to crush your fat-burning and muscle-building goals.

It has been revealed that yes, technically, you can take a pre-workout made with 400 milligrams of caffeine. However, that is the maximum daily dose recommended by the FDA. This means if you’re using a high-stim pre-workout, you may want to avoid caffeine from other sources like coffee, tea, soda, or energy drinks. Since 400 milligrams is the maximum recommended daily dose, I do not advise using a pre-workout containing 600 milligrams of caffeine.

A pre-workout can directly and indirectly make you stronger. A well-dosed pre-workout may help you add a few pounds to your lifts or allow you to push out a few more reps during your workout. However, real strength gains will come from consistent training, proper nutrition, and recovery. If a pre-workout supplement helps you stay consistent in the gym, it may also help you gain strength and muscle mass.

According to recent reports, yes. Depending on your sensitivity to stimulants like caffeine, you may experience side effects, including jitters, anxiety, or difficulty falling asleep. If this is the case, use a half serving or a more moderately dosed pre-workout to assess your tolerance.

The Shokz OpenRun Pro 2 headphones are a real game changer for runners who want great sound without sacrificing safety or comfort. Aly Ellis, our director of content hype, sums it up perfectly: “These are my favorite running headphones ever, specifically, the Kipchoge edition. They get loud enough that you can hear them while running, but you can hear noise and traffic around you. I listen to music, podcasts, and audiobooks while wearing mine, and they all sound great!”.

That open-ear design is the magic here—it keeps you aware of your surroundings, whether you’re dodging bikes on a trail or crossing busy streets.

It has been revealed that sound quality is where the OpenRun Pro 2 really shines, thanks to dual drivers that blend crisp highs from bone conduction with deep bass from air conduction tech, delivering a unique, immersive sound. You get 12 hours of battery life, so you can go for long runs (or even a marathon) without worrying about charging. The fit is secure and stable, with ergonomic ear hooks and a memory wire frame that stays put no matter how much you sweat or move around.

Another standout is the dedicated EQ modes in the Shokz app, letting you tweak your audio for different environments—boost it when it’s noisy, or keep it classic for everyday runs. Calls are crystal clear, even in windy conditions, thanks to dual microphones and smart noise reduction. If you want headphones that sound great, stay comfortable, and keep you safe and aware, the Shokz OpenRun Pro 2 is tough to beat.

The JLab Go Sport+ headphones are a fantastic option for runners and fitness fans who want reliable, sweatproof wireless earbuds without breaking the bank. These earbuds are all about getting the basics right: with an IP55 sweat- and dirt-resistance rating, they can handle even your sweatiest, muddiest workouts. The over-ear hooks and three sizes of silicone ear tips mean you get a secure, comfortable fit—no matter how much you move, these buds stay put without pinching or slipping.

One of the biggest highlights is battery life: You get 9-plus hours per earbud, plus another 26-plus from the charging case, for a whopping 35 hours total. That’s more than enough for a week of workouts, and the integrated USB cable makes recharging the case a breeze. Pairing is simple, especially if you’re on Android thanks to Google Fast Pair, and the connection is rock-solid up to 50 feet away.

The sound quality could be better. It can sound a bit tinny and awkward when you’re expecting something bolder or more rounded. For under $30, though, they’re nothing to laugh at. And with the features and battery life, we think it’s a fair trade.

The JLab Go Sport+ also includes a "Be Aware" mode, which lets in ambient sound so you can stay alert on busy streets or trails. And with the JLab app, you can customize your sound profile and touch controls to suit your preferences. While the audio quality isn’t as rich or dynamic as that of some pricier competitors—think a bit hollow, especially if you’re an audiophile—it’s more than good enough for podcasts, playlists, and calls on the go.

All in all, if you’re after affordable, dependable, and comfortable wireless earbuds for running or the gym, the JLab Go Sport+ is a solid pick that punches above its price point.

Sources indicate that the Beats Powerbeats Pro 2 earbuds are designed to stay put, thanks to flexible earhooks and five ear tip sizes, so you can focus on your run instead of fiddling with your headphones. The IPX4 water resistance means they’ll handle sweat and rain without a hitch.

The sound quality is on point—expect punchy bass and crisp highs (as someone who has worn these, Hamilton has never sounded better), which blend into a nicely balanced sound that makes your playlists pop. Its active noise cancellation and transparency modes are handy, letting you block out the gym clatter and your children’s video game sounds when you want to focus, or let in the world when you’re running on the street and would rather not be taken out by a minivan.

In a recent development, battery life is another big win. You get up to 10 hours per bud (8 if you’re using ANC), and the charging case stretches your total playtime to an astonishing 45 hours. Forgot to charge? No worries—a quick five-minute boost gives you over an hour of listening time.

It has been revealed that there are a few drawbacks: the price is on the higher side, and the latest heart rate monitoring feature isn’t quite polished yet, especially for iPhone users. Plus, there’s no customizable EQ, which might disappoint anyone who likes to fine-tune their sound.

Overall, the Powerbeats Pro 2 are a nice pick if you want secure, great-sounding earbuds that go the distance—just don’t expect them to replace your fitness tracker.

Recent findings suggest that this is the second generation of the Bose Ultra Open earbuds, and I am a huge fan. Both Dengate and I had thousands of miles on the first generation, and this set of buds is proving to hold its own. The improvements are minor, but notable. They include deeper bass, higher volume, more controls, a slightly improved fit, and a better IP rating.

Sources indicate that here’s the thing: most open-ear headphones are something to be desired when it comes to bass and high tones. They can lack richness and that “oomph” you look for when you’re listening to your music. The first generation of the Bose Ultra Open was leaps and bounds above most open-ear, but the bass was still a bit stingy. This set, however, gives you so much more boom for your buck. And you can feel it—seriously—not only is it pumping the sound into your ear, but the vibration is felt in the shell of your ear, which does take some getting used to.

The fit is my second favorite bit of these earbuds. They wrap around the shell of your ear without squeezing or pinching, and they sit gently upon the lower curve above your earlobe. I can and do wear these all day long, taking calls, listening to music, and generally going about my day. The battery life could be better, but for all that sound and comfort, I’m not mad.

The biggest issue with over-the-ear headphones is that sweat can short them out. It’s not all of them; gaming headphones or gaming/multipurpose headphones by and large are designed with sweaty gaming sessions in mind, so they don’t typically short out as often. Casual headphones, on the other hand, have suffered from sweat shock. Not these. These were made with workouts in mind, and they keep all the comfort, all the “leave me alone” energy, and all that great sound. They’re also sweat-resistant and ever so slightly more breathable than your standard over-the-ear cans.

It has been revealed that these are incredibly comfortable, stay put, and the music? It just sounds so glorious. I ran a 20-miler in these, listening to a bunch of film scores, and the music from Interstellar transported me to a place where I didn’t hate myself quite so much. They do, of course, make your ears a bit warm after you’ve been wearing them a while, but honestly? I was running at elevation (over 8,000 feet) and I actually loved both the warmth and the wind protection they provided me. And they sounded just as good at two and a half hours as they did at minute one of charge.

In a recent development, apple’s AirPods Pro 3 are the gold standard for wireless earbuds, and also the most ubiquitous. They’re the overwhelming favorite earbuds on the market. I think that’s largely because the moment you pop them in, you notice the comfortable, secure fit (thanks to four ear tip sizes) and Apple’s signature ergonomic design. Whether you’re commuting, running, or just trying to listen to your romance novel audiobook without scandalizing your family, these buds stay put and feel featherlight.

Thanks to a custom high-excursion driver and Apple's H2 chip, your hype music comes in sharp and booming, even in loud environments. Apple's active noise cancellation is among the best of the best, and adaptive transparency mode lets you hear what’s going on around you at a level you can stand when you’re trying to get your workout on. Adaptive audio and conversation awareness are upcoming in this version and automatically blend ANC and transparency, or lower your volume when you start talking. Personally, I didn’t notice this sound degradation, but my husband says it’s noticeable to him.

Industry observers note that battery life is pretty good—up to 10 hours per bud and 24 hours total with the little white case. The case itself is instantly recognizable, supports wireless and USB-C charging, and even has a speaker and Find My integration for those inevitable “where did I put them?” moments. (And not for anything, there’s about a million ways to customize these if you’re on Etsy.) They’re also IPX4 rated, so they’ll handle sweat and a little rain, though they’re not meant for swimming laps like the Suunto Aqua.

The live translate feature is cool, but testing it with my Mandarin-speaking husband revealed lags and a few glitches. (And, well, some things translated very oddly, and not in a good way.) The heart rate function is similar. It's better than my watch, but not as good as a chest strap, and I think that's pretty fair, honestly.

They aren’t perfect, though. The case scratches easily, and you get the best experience only with Apple devices. Still, for iPhone users who want top-tier sound, seamless controls, and noise cancellation that actually works, the AirPods Pro 3 will be an obvious go-to for many runners.

Industry observers note that the Sony Sport Earbuds are cute and unbelievably comfy, especially in the eye-catching pink colorway that adds a fun pop to your gear. The marbled case is a stylish bonus in my opinion (yes, it's twee; no, I don't care). These earbuds stayed perfectly put and cozy during a four-hour, 30-mile run—no slipping, no discomfort.The noise-canceling tech blocks out distractions so you can fully dive into your music, though they’re not the best for driving since they quiet things down too much, even in transparency mode. Touch controls feel smooth, with volume adjusting in tiny, gentle steps—no sudden bursts to startle your ears. Sound quality is crisp and lively thanks to dynamic drivers, and Bluetooth 5.3 keeps the connection rock solid. Battery life is marathon-ready, lasting up to 8 hours with noise canceling on. These buds combine cuteness, comfort, and serious performance for anyone on the move.

In a recent development, I’m never going to do a triathlon, because bicycles are terrifying, but swimming? Sweating? Those I do. And listen, because of my disgustingly sweaty head and love of the water, I’ve dunked a lot of headphones in the name of journalism, and most of them did not survive the experience. The H2O Audio Tri 2 Pro ($199) took every chlorine-ridden and sweat-soaked hour.

According to recent reports, the headphones' IPX8 rating is 12 feet, making submersion time effectively unlimited, which means they outlast me in the pool or the ocean (yes, I love open-water swimming by a considerable margin). The bone conduction design pairs with earplugs for genuinely decent underwater audio. It has real bass response, not the sad tinny thumping you’d expect. As someone who prefers to run to a mix of T. Swift and My Chemical Romance, I like it to sound as emotional as possible to keep me motivated.

But the Playlist+ feature is what sets this set of cans apart from others: you can download eight gigabytes of music directly to your headphones, so you can leave your phone in the pool locker or locked in your car—your playlist is ready to go the second you jump in. No phone, no Bluetooth dropouts, no excuses. On land, the sound is firmly good enough, and yes, the buttons need a firmware lesson in responsiveness. But for swimmers and sweaty eddies? This thing is a boss.

Shokz leveled up with this pair of headphones. For years, they’ve been known primarily for their stellar bone-conduction headphones, but with these noise-canceling, open-ear hooks, they’re shifting the narrative for their brand. Černá tried these as well. “I was pretty skeptical at first—no way these earbuds could withstand all the bouncing while I run and not move,” she stated. “Surprise: they don’t bounce around! It’s almost as if they’re magnetically attached to my ear.".

Recent findings suggest that thanks to the dual noise-canceling microphones embedded in the headphones, they were audible in a variety of conditions, including some heavy wind. A feature Černá loves is the smart wear function, which turns the phones off when you’re not wearing them, keeping your place in your audiobook or podcast. And for the ADHD-addled, like myself? Being able to ping your earbuds is honestly so clutch. Forget where they are? Don’t worry, you can find them.

They’re comfy, they can handle a decent amount of sweat and precipitation, they’re feature-rich, and honestly, just a great experience overall.

Choosing the right running headphones can really make your run. With so many options available, it’s important to consider which features are most important for your needs. To help guide your decision, here are some key factors to consider when selecting the perfect running headphones.

It has been revealed that in-ear headphones, also known as earbuds, fit directly into the ear canal. They are often compact and lightweight, making them highly portable. In-ear headphones can offer good sound isolation, blocking out some external noise and, depending on the fit, a decent level of bass. They often come with various ear tip sizes to make sure they’re not going to fall out of your ears.

Hook headphones typically feature a design with hooks that wrap around the ears for added stability. This makes them popular for activities like running or exercising, where a secure fit is crucial to prevent them from falling out. Hook headphones can come in various styles, including earbuds with hooks and over-ear, open-ear styles with hooks.

Sources indicate that bone conduction headphones work by transmitting sound vibrations through the bones of your skull, bypassing the eardrums. This allows you to listen to audio while keeping your ears open to your surroundings. This is especially useful for runners who need to be aware of traffic or other environmental sounds.

It has been revealed that open-ear headphones are designed to sit outside the ear, allowing you to hear both your audio and the environment around you. They don't block your ear canal, so you remain aware of your surroundings, which is helpful for safety during outdoor activities. However, they may leak sound, and the audio quality might not be as immersive as other types.

Headphones with storage typically include onboard memory for storing music files directly on the headphones. This eliminates the need to carry a separate device for music playback. This feature is particularly convenient for runners or swimmers who prefer not to bring their phones along.

Industry observers note that while our testers experienced no immediate complications with water or sweat damage, prolonged exposure to moisture and salt can harm earbuds not designed to repel these elements. That’s why we found it imperative that we checked out each device’s “IP,” or ”Ingress Protection” rating. This rating consists of two digits:.

Noise Cancellation vs Ambient Awareness.

Sources indicate that picking between noise cancellation and ambient awareness for your running headphones is like choosing your own adventure. If you're dodging chatty pedestrians in the urban jungle, ambient awareness—whether that be found in typical earbuds or open-ear style headphones—might be your best bet, keeping you alert to honks and “behind you” shouts. But if you’re hitting the serene trails, craving that deep focus, or you have really noisy coworkers or hate the sound of grunting gym bros, let noise cancellation be your peaceful respite, blocking out everything but the sound of your own steady rhythm and, perhaps, a suspenseful podcast.

Recent findings suggest that battery life is essential for running headphones, especially for long distances. Will these headphones endure the entirety of your week’s run plan without dying? I’m terrible at remembering to charge my stuff, so this is crucial for folks like me.

Connectivity is also important. Most running headphones use Bluetooth, and the range can vary. Ideally, you want a stable connection that won't drop out when your phone is a few steps away. Typical Bluetooth range is around 30 feet, but interference can reduce this. Some newer headphones offer improved Bluetooth versions for greater range and stability.

Sources indicate that headphones, like other gadgets, have firmware that controls their functions and features. Manufacturers often release updates to improve performance, add new features, or fix complications with firmware, which can have bugs or limitations like any software. These updates are crucial for maintaining optimal functionality and ensuring compatibility with the latest devices and technologies.

Industry observers note that many of today's best headphones and earbuds have companion apps that allow consumers to manage and enhancement the firmware. Additionally, these updates may introduce newly introduced features (e.g., enhanced noise cancellation, improved call quality, and more customization options), all of which are managed through the partner app. Keeping the firmware up to date via the app ensures that the headphones perform optimally and offer the latest features.

It has been revealed that when it comes to running headphones, durability is honestly everything, because, who wants to buy a latest pair every few months? Trust us, our team put these headphones through the wringer, testing them for weeks, sometimes even months and years (yep, we’re that dedicated) to find the ones that can actually keep up with your miles. We sweated on them, dropped them, stuffed them in gym bags, and even braved a few surprise rain showers—just to make sure they’re as tough as your training routine. So, when we say these are the best running headphones for durability, you know we mean it.

In a recent development, to pinpoint the best running headphones, our team put each pair through thorough, real-world testing for weeks—and sometimes even months. (And not for anything, I’ve had a pair of the original Beats Pro for five years, and they’re still rocking.) We had all kinds of runners try them out, from marathoners to casual joggers, to make sure our results would work for everyone. This way, we got feedback on comfort, fit, and performance for every running style and distance.

Our tests weren’t just in one spot; we put these headphones through all sorts of situations to see how tough and functional they really are. This meant running in different weather, from sunshine to sudden downpours, and at various elevations to check their performance under varying physical stresses. We also tested them in places with different noise levels—from quiet trails where you don’t need to hear much around you, to busy city streets where safety and clear sound are super important.

Through this rigorous evaluation, we were able to pinpoint headphones that could withstand sweat, accidental drops, and general wear and tear associated with regular running. We paid close attention to factors like secure fit, battery life, sound quality, and the effectiveness of features like noise cancellation and ambient awareness in real-world scenarios.

How do you listen to music and run phone-free?

As a loyal Garmin user, I recommend using models like the Forerunner 170 Music edition. The latter has more features if you’re a multi-sport, stats-junkie, but the price is significantly higher. The watches allow you to sync with music providers, such as Spotify. Most earbuds, with the exception of Apple Airpods, are Garmin compatible.

How do you pair wireless earbuds to your Garmin?

Test Editor Morgan Petruny offers a helpful guide on pairing your earbuds to devices. Here are her instructions on pairing them to you Garmin:.

Sources indicate that for a deep clean, fill a glass with a drop of dish soap in half a cup of warm water. Remove the foam or silicone tips from the earbuds, and let them soak in the soap mixture for 30 minutes. Use a cotton swab or Q-Tip to remove excess particles. Allow the tips to air dry before screwing them back on. Use a clean old toothbrush to gently scrub the actual earbuds, mesh cover pointed down.
